title: Teams, Zoom & meetings
blurb: Can't hear or be heard, camera off, screen share, Teams won't start.

remedies.title: Teams won't open, is blank, or keeps loading
remedies.why: Teams' saved data got damaged, or an old and a new Teams are fighting.

steps.text: Quit Teams completely (right-click its icon in the taskbar/menu bar › Quit) and open it again.
Clear Teams' cache and settings (you stay signed in to your account; chats are on the server).
Clear the cache: quit Teams, then in Finder › Go › Go to Folder open ~/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.com.microsoft.teams and move the folder to the Bin; reopen Teams.
Try Teams in the browser (teams.microsoft.com); if it works there, reinstall the app.

remedies.escalate: Tell IT whether Teams in the browser works.

remedies.title: Teams sign-in error or wrong account
remedies.why: Teams keeps your Microsoft sign-in shared with Office; a damaged or mixed-up sign-in breaks it.

steps.text: Click your picture in Teams › Add another account, or Sign out and sign in with the right one.
Clear Teams' cache.
See "Microsoft 365 sign-in loops" for removing saved sign-ins.

remedies.title: People in the meeting can't hear me
remedies.why: You're muted (in the app or on the headset), the wrong microphone is picked, or the system blocks apps from the microphone.

steps.text: Check the mute button in the meeting and on your headset or its cable.
In the meeting's device settings (Teams: ⋯ › Settings › Device settings; Zoom: ^ next to Mute), pick the microphone you're actually using.
Allow apps to use the microphone: Privacy & security › Microphone › on for desktop apps.
Allow the app: Privacy & Security › Microphone › turn on Teams/Zoom, then restart it.
Speak and watch the input level in Sound settings; if it doesn't move, the microphone isn't picking you up.
Speak and watch the input level in Sound settings › Input.

remedies.title: I can't hear anyone in the meeting
remedies.why: The meeting app plays to a different speaker or headset, or the app's own volume is down.

steps.text: In the meeting's device settings pick the speaker or headset you're using, and play the test sound.
Check the app isn't muted in the volume mixer.
Pick the right output in Sound settings › Output.
Unplug and replug the headset; for Bluetooth, see the Bluetooth headset remedy.

remedies.title: Camera doesn't work in Teams or Zoom
remedies.why: Another app holds the camera, the system blocks the app, or a privacy shutter/switch is closed.

steps.text: Check for a sliding cover or camera key on the laptop (often F8 or F10 with a camera icon).
Close other apps that might use the camera, then pick the right camera in the meeting's device settings.
Allow apps to use the camera.
Allow the app: Privacy & Security › Camera › turn on Teams/Zoom, then restart it.

remedies.title: Screen sharing shows black or doesn't work
remedies.why: On a Mac the app needs Screen Recording permission; on Windows protected video or graphics settings can black out the share.

steps.text: Allow the app: Privacy & Security › Screen & System Audio Recording › turn on Teams/Zoom, then quit and reopen it.
Share one window instead of the whole screen, or the whole screen instead of a window.
Streaming video sites and some secure apps black themselves out on purpose.
On laptops with two graphics chips, setting the meeting app to the power-saving GPU can fix black shares: Settings › System › Display › Graphics.

remedies.title: Echo or feedback in a meeting
remedies.why: Someone's speakers are playing into their microphone, or two devices in the same room joined with audio.

steps.text: Use a headset instead of laptop speakers.
If several people are in one room, only one device should join with audio; the others join with audio off.
Turn down speaker volume and turn on noise suppression in the meeting app's settings.

remedies.title: Meeting video freezes or audio breaks up
remedies.why: The internet connection can't keep up (often Wi-Fi), or the computer is overloaded.

steps.text: Turn off your video when quality drops; it frees a lot of bandwidth.
Move closer to the router, or use a cable.
Pause cloud sync and big downloads during calls.
Close other heavy apps and browser tabs.

remedies.title: Teams notifications don't show
remedies.why: Teams' own notification settings, the system's Focus / Do Not Disturb, or the system blocking Teams' notifications.

steps.text: Teams › Settings › Notifications and activity: check chats and mentions are set to Banner.
Turn off Do not disturb / Focus, and check Teams is allowed to notify.
Turn off Focus and allow Microsoft Teams in Notifications.
Make sure your Teams status isn't set to Do not disturb.

remedies.title: "Teams Meeting" button missing in Outlook
remedies.why: The Teams add-in for Outlook didn't load or was disabled.

steps.text: Make sure the Teams app is installed and you're signed in, then restart Outlook.
In classic Outlook: File › Options › Add-ins › Manage COM Add-ins › tick Microsoft Teams Meeting Add-in.
Schedule from Teams' own Calendar, or Outlook on the web, meanwhile.

remedies.title: Zoom says I need to update to join
remedies.why: Zoom requires a recent version to join meetings.

steps.text: Open Zoom › your picture › Check for Updates.
If the update fails, download the latest from zoom.us/download and install over it.
Join from the browser instead: in the meeting link page choose "Join from your browser".
